name: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR T-CELL (CAR-T) THERAPY
indication: CAR-T therapy with Tisacel (Tisagenlecleucel) for the treatment of paediatric and young adult patients up to and including 25 years of age with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) that is refractory, in relapse post-transplant or in second or later relapse.

drugs.special_instructions: Will be dose banded according to the national dose band (25mg/ml).

Will be dose banded according to national dose banding table (20mg/ml). Lymphodepleting chemotherapy may be omitted if a patient is experiencing significant cytopenia, e.g., white blood cell (WBC) count <1.0 x10⁹cells/ L within one week prior to infusion.

Single-course therapy — not a repeating cycle. Lymphodepletion days -6 to -3, CAR-T infusion day 0. Product range: 1.2 x 10^6 to 6 x 10^8 cells per treatment dose. Target dose: Patients 50kg and below: 0.2 to 5 x 10^6 cells / kg body weight. Patients above 50kg: 0.1 to 2.5 x 10^8 cells (non-weight based). One individual treatment dose comprises 1 or more infusion bags. Each infusion bag may contain either 10-30ml (50ml bag) or 30-50ml (250ml bag) cell dispersion. Cells are cryopreserved and require thawing prior to administration — see WBMT SOP P-P-78. Administer gravimetrically, not via a volumetric pump. Administer via a latex-free giving set without a leukocyte depleting filter and primed with sodium chloride 0.9%. Infuse within 30 minutes of thaw completion time. Infuse over a maximum of 30 minutes. The start and stop time of infusion must be documented, including any interruption. Gently agitate the bag during infusion to prevent cell clumping. If the volume to be administered is ≤20 mL, intravenous push may be used as an alternative method of administration. All contents of the infusion bag(s) should be infused. If more than one infusion bag is received, the next bag should only be thawed after the contents of the preceding bag have been infused. Once the full volume has been administered, rinse the tubing at the same rate with 10-30ml 0.9% sodium chloride solution to ensure all Tisacel is delivered. Once completed, the infusion bag(s) and giving set must be disposed of in clinical waste, in accordance with Trust policy. If the bag is not fully administered, this must be documented, and the consultant and pharmacist notified. The manufacturer must be informed and the remaining Tisacel discarded in clinical waste with their approval. A GM spill-kit must be transported with Tisacel and available on the ward of administration. Local procedures must be followed in the event of a spill. Tisacel contains genetically modified (GM) human blood cells — exposure must be avoided; adhere to handling, PPE, spills, and waste disposal procedures. CAR-T administration should not occur out of core hours or over a weekend.

take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Can be administered oral or intravenous. Prophylactic antiemetic. Started on first day of lymphodepletion and continued as required.
Can be administered oral or intravenous. Prophylactic antiemetic. Started on first day of lymphodepletion and continued as required.
Starting on first day of lymphodepletion (Day -6). Continue twice daily until neutrophil recovery.
Starting on first day of lymphodepletion (Day -6). Continue once daily until neutrophil recovery or switch to posaconazole if prolonged neutropenia or prior invasive fungal infection.

Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) prophylaxis — nebulised 300mg during lymphodepletion at consultant advice, when co-trimoxazole cannot be given due to neutropenia. To be continued every 28 days until count recovery sufficient for co-trimoxazole use.

Anti-infective prophylaxis — use if prolonged neutropenia or previous invasive fungal infection (in place of or in addition to fluconazole). Start on day of lymphodepletion (Day -6) and continue once daily.
To commence on first day of lymphodepletion until platelet count >50 x10⁹/L. Specific drug will be determined by consultant.
Mouthwash, according to local or national policy on the treatment of mucositis. Start on day of lymphodepletion (Day -6) and continue.
Mouthwash, according to local or national policy on the treatment of mucositis. Start on day of lymphodepletion (Day -6) and continue.

Seizure prophylaxis — may be considered due to neurotoxicity risk associated with Tisacel, or if patient has a history of seizures. 500mg twice daily orally commencing Day 0 until Day +30. For weaning: reduce to 250mg twice daily orally for two weeks, then 250mg once daily for one week, then stop.

Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) prophylaxis, prescribed according to individual patient TLS risk and at consultant review. Must start on the day of lymphodepletion and be re-reviewed on the day of Tisacel infusion.

rescue_medications.special_instructions: Maximum 800mg per dose. Administer 8mg/kg (maximum 800mg) intravenously 8-hourly if required — maximum of four doses. Must be prescribed as when required in advance of CAR-T infusion, in the event of CRS. Four doses must be available on the ward prior to Tisacel infusion. Follow local procedures for administration.
Can be administered under the supervision of a doctor for the treatment of rigors.

rescue_medications.frequency: Four times a day when required
rescue_medications.special_instructions: When required for the treatment of fluid overload. Can be administered oral or intravenous.
Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) prophylaxis. Administer once a day as needed per individual TLS risk.

dose_modifications.description: CrCl >50 ml/min: 100% of original cyclophosphamide dose.
Creatinine Clearance 30-50 ml/min: reduce dose to 75% of original dose.
Creatinine Clearance < 30 ml/min: high dose therapy not generally undertaken.
CrCl >70 ml/min: 100% of original fludarabine dose.
Creatinine Clearance 50-69 ml/min: reduce dose by 20%.
Creatinine Clearance 30-49 ml/min: reduce dose by 40%.
Creatinine Clearance < 30 ml/min: contraindicated (do not use fludarabine, consider alternative lymphodepletion regimen).
No dose modification is recommended for hepatic dysfunction in those receiving fludarabine.
dose_modifications.action_text: Full dose fludarabine — no hepatic dose modification required

dose_modifications.description: Severe hepatic impairment may be associated with decreased activation of cyclophosphamide. This may alter the effectiveness and should be considered when selecting and interpreting the dose. Discuss with consultant.
dose_modifications.action_text: Discuss cyclophosphamide dose with consultant — severe hepatic impairment may reduce drug activation

dose_modifications.description: If there are signs of possible disease relapse, confirm with consultant before proceeding with lymphodepleting chemotherapy.
dose_modifications.action_text: Confirm with consultant before proceeding — signs of possible disease relapse

monitoring: FBC, U&Es, renal, liver and bone, CRP, coagulation screen, ferritin and LDH prior to initiating treatment and daily thereafter.
Screening for HBV, HCV and HIV must be performed before collection of cells for Tisagenlecleucel manufacture.
Echocardiogram and baseline measure of lung function must be taken prior to initiating lymphodepletion.
Temperature, blood pressure and oxygen saturation monitored 4-hourly after Tisacel administration on Day 0 and then twice daily as directed in accordance with local procedures.

CRS: Monitor for symptoms including pyrexia, tiredness, cardiac failure, tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, dyspnoea, hypoxia, capillary leak syndrome, chills, renal impairment, headache, malaise, transaminitis, nausea, diarrhoea, hypotension. Nearly all patients treated with Tisacel experience some degree of CRS, including life-threatening and fatal reactions.
CRS graded on the WBMT CRS Assessment Form in the patient's notes. See WBMT Policy P-G-1 and SOP P-P-78 and P-P-79 for monitoring requirements.

ICANS: Monitor for symptoms including seizures, somnolence, headaches, confusion, agitation, speech disorders, tremor, encephalopathy, ataxia, memory impairment, mental status changes, hallucinations, depressed level of consciousness, delirium, dysmetria.
ICE score of the patient must be assessed twice daily and documented on the WBMT ICE Assessment Form in the patient's notes.
warnings: This regimen will only be available to prescribe at the Wessex Blood and Marrow Transplant Unit.
Lymphodepleting chemotherapy must be administered prior to Tisacel.
This protocol includes both lymphodepletion and CAR-T administration. For autologous use only.

If the patient has experienced a previous Grade 4 haemorrhagic cystitis with cyclophosphamide, or demonstrated a chemo refractory state to a cyclophosphamide-containing regimen administered shortly before lymphodepleting chemotherapy, consider alternative cytarabine and etoposide -containing regimen: Tisacel –Cytarabine (500) – Etoposide (150).

Patients treated with fludarabine carry a lifelong risk of transfusion associated graft versus host disease (TA-GVHD). Where blood products are required, these patients must receive ONLY IRRADIATED BLOOD PRODUCTS for life. Ensure transfusion departments are notified and the patient has been issued with an alert card to carry with them at all times.
Symptoms of CRS or ICANS can occur weeks after infusion and therefore the patient must be issued with an alert card to carry with them at all times.

Any suspected adverse reaction to a CAR-T cell infusion should be reported. Reporting forms and information can be found at – www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard. Consideration should also be given to reporting adverse events to the relevant manufacturer via their usual channels.

Prophylactic use of systemic corticosteroids is not recommended as it may interfere with the activity of the cellular therapy and therefore, they should not be administered as part of the pre-medication. However, corticosteroids may be used in the treatment of CRS or ICANS under consultant advice.

Cautions with Tisacel treatment: Unresolved serious adverse reactions (especially pulmonary reactions, cardiac reactions, or hypotension) from preceding chemotherapies. Active uncontrolled infection or inflammatory disease. Active GVHD.
Lymphodepleting chemotherapy may be omitted if a patient is experiencing significant cytopenia, e.g., white blood cell (WBC) count <1.0 x10⁹cells/ L within one week prior to infusion.
Lymphodepleting regimen must only be started after availability of Tisacel is confirmed.
Fludarabine will be dose banded according to the national dose band (25mg/ml).
Cyclophosphamide will be dose banded in accordance with national dose banding table (20mg/ml).

A minimum period of time must elapse between last dose of conditioning chemotherapy and CAR-T infusion, and a longer period is required for patients with renal insufficiency. This information can be found on the patient's CAR-T cell schedule.
CAR-T administration should not occur out of core hours or over a weekend.

Tisacel contains genetically modified (GM) human blood cells. Exposure to Tisacel must be avoided. Procedures for handling, personal protective equipment, spills and waste disposal must be adhered to.

Local guidelines on handling of waste of human-derived-materials must be followed in case of accidental exposure. Work surfaces and materials which have potentially been in contact with Tisacel must be decontaminated with approved disinfectants.

See WBMT SOP P-P-78 (CAR-T and IEC infusion procedure), SOP P-P-79 (Immune effector cells policy), and Policy P-G-1 (Patient monitoring after CAR-T cell infusion) for monitoring requirements and further administration direction.
Extravasation classification: Fludarabine — non-vesicant. Cyclophosphamide — non-vesicant.
Nearly all patients treated with Tisacel experience some degree of CRS, including life-threatening and fatal reactions.
Ensure patient has been issued with a Tisacel treatment alert card prior to administration.

On Day -6, check: antibacterials, antifungals and antivirals are prescribed in accordance with the individual CAR-T schedule; four doses of tocilizumab are available on the ward; supportive medications are prescribed.
